description: Updates downtown zoning for building height and street design.

segments.title: Overview of Proposed Changes and Engagement
description: Brief overview of proposed downtown zoning changes.
Engagement began 2023 with focus groups.
Public engagement launched summer 2024.
Detailed information available on saskatoon.ca/downtownzoning.

chips.text: Engagement phase ongoing, targeting early 2025 stakeholder sessions.
Final amendments and report to council targeted for Q2 2025.

segments.title: B6 District General Changes
description: B6 is downtown's primary zone for high-density uses.
Zone fundamentals are sound, but improvements identified.
Changes grouped into broad topic areas.

segments.title: B6 Street Interface Regulations
description: Regulations concern how buildings relate to streets.
Proposing tweaks and new rules for ground floor active uses.
Require transparent openings and public entrances.
Prohibiting drive-throughs in downtown zones.

chips.text: Prohibiting drive-through service windows in downtown B6, M4, and MX2 zones.

segments.title: B6 Building Height and Form Regulations Overview
description: Significant overhaul proposed for open volume regulations.
Adjustments for residential setbacks to align with other zones.
Maintain building step-back requirements for street facades.
Add screening requirements for rooftop mechanical equipment.

segments.title: B6 Adaptive Reuse Regulations
description: B6 zone permits broad land uses, few regulatory barriers.
Permit small-scale artisan and food manufacturing.
Waive setback requirements for non-residential to residential conversions.

chips.text: Developers converting older non-residential buildings to residential uses.

segments.title: Detailed Open Volume Changes
description: Open volume governs building height and massing related to site size.
Current graph difficult to interpret, limiting for small sites.
Proposed changes simplify graph, increase development rates.
Permit six-story buildings on all B6 sites without open volume.

chips.text: Permitting six-story buildings on all B6 sites without open volume.
Small to medium site developers in the B6 zone.

segments.title: Downtown Surface Parking Regulations
description: Regulations apply to B6, M4, and MX2 downtown zones.
Distinguish temporary (up to 6 years) and permanent lots.
Prohibit surface parking on 21st Street and 2nd Avenue.
Higher site improvement expectations for permanent parking.

chips.text: Property owners with surface parking lots in downtown B6, M4, MX2 zones.
Regulations aim to improve urban environment quality, reduce negative effects.

segments.title: Project Next Steps and Timeline
description: Currently in engagement phase, stakeholder sessions early 2025.
Final amendments to be reported to MPC and City Council.
Targeting second quarter of 2025 for decision.

chips.text: Final amendments and report to council targeted for Q2 2025.

segments.title: Q&A: Mechanical Screening Requirements
description: Question about parameters for mechanical screening on rooftops.
Administration states screening for visible equipment, no height thresholds.
Councillor raises concerns about significant cost and structural implications.

chips.text: Councillor flags significant cost and structural implications of blanket mechanical screening.
Specific parameters for mechanical screening requirements remain undefined.

segments.title: Q&A: Residential Setback Inclusions
description: Councillor asks about value of setbacks for new residential buildings.
Administration explains harmonization with other high-density zones.
Staff notes setbacks have financial implication on construction costs.

chips.text: Staff notes setbacks have financial implications on construction costs.

segments.title: Q&A: Building Base, Middle, Top Division
description: Councillor questions value of base-middle-top division for tall buildings.
Administration emphasizes importance for city scale and facade articulation.

chips.text: Councillor questions the value of base-middle-top division for very tall buildings.

segments.title: Q&A: Adaptive Reuse (Manufacturing Regulation)
description: Councillor asks about city's role in regulating small-scale manufacturing.
Administration states city has regulatory levers through development permits.
Business licensing also serves as a trigger for review.

chips.text: City regulates homecraft and food production through development permits and business licensing.

description: Report details proposed downtown B6 zoning changes.
Includes rules for parking, building height, adaptive reuse.

chips.text: Received as information
Downtown surface parking lot owners were directly notified about potential zoning changes.
The timeline for temporary parking lots to cease operations after expiry is not yet defined.
Staff committed to holding public engagement sessions for stakeholders in early 2025.

segments.title: New Surface Parking Regulations
description: New regulations distinguish temporary and permanent surface parking.
Both are discretionary uses in light teal areas.
Prohibited on 21st Street and Second Avenue frontages.
Temporary parking has low site improvement expectations (6 years). Permanent parking requires higher site improvements.

chips.text: Engagement sessions planned for early 2025, report to Council Q2 2025.
New regulations distinguish temporary and permanent surface parking.
Property owners with surface parking lots in downtown.

segments.title: Mechanical Screening and Entertainment District Zoning
description: Question raised about parameters for mechanical screening.
Developer flexibility needed due to significant screening costs.
Staff acknowledged balancing expectations with viable development.
Direct control district is being explored for the Entertainment District.

chips.text: Councillor flags significant cost of mechanical screening for developers.
Direct control district explored for Entertainment District zoning.

segments.title: Residential Setback Requirements
description: Question on setbacks for new residential buildings versus adaptive reuse.
Staff explained harmonizing and decreasing downtown setbacks.
Adaptive reuse of existing buildings gets setback exceptions.
Setbacks have financial implications on construction costs.

chips.text: Setback exceptions for adaptive reuse of existing buildings.
Staff notes financial implications of setbacks on construction costs.

segments.title: Building Form and Density Bonuses
description: Question about base-middle-top division for tall buildings.
Staff explained principle for legible components, breaking down scale.
Councillor praised open volume increases and density bonuses.
Density bonuses incentivize public realm improvements.

chips.text: Councillor praises density bonuses for public realm improvements.

segments.title: Flexibility for Mechanical Screening
description: Chair revisited discussion on mechanical screening.
Councillor reiterated support for flexibility based on visibility.

chips.text: Councillor supports flexibility for mechanical screening based on visibility.

segments.title: Residential Setbacks for Density
description: Chair revisited residential setback requirements.
Councillor supported reducing dimensions for increased density.
Reducing red tape for existing building conversions is positive.

chips.text: Councillor supports reduced setbacks to increase downtown density.

segments.title: Ground Floor Retail and Accessibility
description: Question about ground floor retail flexibility and winter benefits.
Staff broadened requirements to include publicly accessible areas.
Zoning bylaw does not detail accessibility, building code regulates it.
City will ensure zoning doesn't contradict accessibility standards.

chips.text: Ground floor requirements broadened to include public lobbies, multi-purpose areas.
Specific plans for exterior accessibility network not addressed.

segments.title: Ground Floor Flexibility and Drive-Through Prohibition
description: Councillor praised flexibility for ground floor uses.
Prohibition of downtown drive-throughs was supported.
Drive-throughs include service windows and ATMs.
Walk-up windows are not prohibited and are good for downtown.

chips.text: Drive-through service windows (including ATMs) prohibited downtown.
Councillor 'loves' the prohibition of downtown drive-throughs.

segments.title: Signage and Advertising Regulations
description: Concern raised about blank walls, signage, and advertising regulations.
Downtown signage regulations are currently liberal.
Billboards and digital signs are not compatible with downtown.
Evolving sign regulations is not part of current scope.

chips.text: No current proposals for evolving downtown signage regulations.

segments.title: Multiple Principal Buildings on Downtown Sites
description: Question about examples of multiple principal buildings on one site.
River Landing cited as an example of integrated urban development.
Intent is to avoid suburban power center format.
Regulations aim to remove barriers for such developments.

chips.text: Regulations to allow and guide multiple principal buildings on one site.

segments.title: New Regulations and Development Incentives
description: New regulations apply to new development, not existing structures.
Existing buildings become non-conforming but can continue.
Additions or expansions to existing buildings must comply.
No specific incentives for these regulations, but broader incentives exist.

chips.text: Owners of existing non-conforming downtown buildings.
Subdivision and levies waived for residential development.
